case_name: Smt. Arathi @ Bharathi Prabhudeva vs Smt. Geeta @ Bharati W/O Late Prabhudev

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Arathi @ Bharathi Prabhudeva (mother and natural guardian)
parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Geeta @ Bharati W/O Late Prabhudev (mother) and children (Kum. Megghana, Kum. Adithya)

facts_of_case: The parties are the mother and natural guardian of three minor children. The trial court partly decreed a suit filed by the respondent for declaration and to set aside an earlier judgment.

legal_principles.principle: The court's discretion in granting custody to a natural guardian is not unfettered and must be exercised judiciously.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that the court's discretion in granting custody to a natural guardian is not unfettered and must be exercised judiciously, having regard to the best interests of the child.

legal_principles.principle: The court's primary concern in granting custody is the best interests of the child.
legal_principles.held: This Court holds that the primary concern in granting custody to a natural guardian or otherwise, is the best interests of the child.

outcome.final_order: The appeal was dismissed as the appellant failed to comply with an earlier order dated 15.12.2010.

keywords: Section 7 Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act
Section 12 Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act
use_for_drafting: advising on joint vs sole custody
